newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott - Republicans move on tax cut offer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott - Republicans move on tax cut offer.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Thursday Republicans "could live with" a five-year tax cut of $140 billion, well down from the $190 billion initially proposed by the party.

Republicans have made an offer to the White House on tax cuts and spending as part of the ongoing balanced budget negotiations and are now waiting for the Democrats and President Clinton to respond with a counter-offer, he said.

Asked if Republicans had offered to accept a $140 billion tax cut, Lott told reporters, "We could live with that." The amount is still well above the $98 billion tax cut proposed by President Clinton. The administration also sought to offset the tax reductions with $72 billion in tax increases.
"They are still wanting less than we can agree to. We are saying we realize we are probably not going to get it in the $197 billion range," Lott said.

"I think we are working toward each other. They are coming up, we are coming down," he added. Republicans have insisted the tax cut package include lower rates on capital gains taxes, a child care tax credit and relief from inheritance taxes.
Lott said he still expected to discuss the budget with Clinton soon even though the president will be out of town early next week. "We are going to communicate on Tuesday," he said.

He stressed the importance of the budget negotiations, which he said would have a longer-lasting impact on relations between Congress and the White House than other controversies including the current battle over ratification of the Chemical Weapons Treaty.

"More important for the long-range atmosphere in the Senate and the relationship between us and the administration is going to be determined more by the budget than by this," he said if the treaty vote coming up Thursday.
